The failing test case [`DateUtilsTest.testTruncateLang59`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_65_group_c_arch/src/test/org/apache/commons/lang/time/DateUtilsTest.java#L894-L962) and its associated operations in [`DateUtils`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_65_group_c_arch/src/java/org/apache/commons/lang/time/DateUtils.java#L542-L713) have been investigated.

### Findings
* **Failure Trigger**: In `MST7MDT` (Mountain Time), October 31, 2004 marks the daylight saving time fall-back changeover where the 01:00 hour occurs twice (first MDT, then MST).
* **Observed Behavior**: Truncating or rounding a date (`2004-10-31 01:02:03.004 MDT`) to fields such as `Calendar.SECOND`, `Calendar.MINUTE`, `Calendar.HOUR`, or `Calendar.DATE` erroneously shifts the resulting date from Mountain Daylight Time (`MDT`) to Mountain Standard Time (`MST`), advancing the timestamp by 1 hour.
* **Intended Behavior**: Truncation and rounding operations must modify only the targeted lower fields while preserving the original Daylight Saving Time status/offset and not shifting the time by an hour.

The black-box behavior specification has been written to [requirement.feature](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/lang_65_group_c_arch/requirement.feature).
